title: Encodings and Compression: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Encodings and Compression: Visual Guide

1. Two Layers Of Shrink | one status column stepped from 8 MB raw through dictionary encoding, RLE and a codec, with the byte count at each stage | encodings are type-aware and do the intelligent work while codecs only see bytes and mop up, so a heavy codec on a well-encoded column buys percent rather than multiples

2. The Cardinality Cliff | a slider over distinct values showing bits per row and the point where the dictionary page overflows and the writer falls back to plain encoding | dictionary cost grows only logarithmically with cardinality, but the dictionary itself must fit a page, and the silent mid-chunk fallback explains sudden file-size jumps

3. Sorted Pays Twice | the same status column written sorted and in arrival order, with run counts, encoded size and pruning quality | one write-time sort decision feeds two separate mechanisms, lengthening RLE runs and narrowing row-group min/max at the same time

4. Where The Bottleneck Is | five codecs timed over a 10 GB scan on object storage and on local NVMe, with I/O and decompression shown as overlapping segments | heavier compression wins when I/O-bound and loses when CPU-bound, and write-once read-many makes decompression speed the number that matters

5. Postings, Renamed | four one-to-one mappings between inverted-index compression and Parquet encodings, plus where the two genuinely differ | both apply a cheap reversible transform that exposes low entropy and both are fuelled by sortedness, differing only in access pattern
